name: How long does it take to remove tree roots from a sewer line?

mainEntity.name: How long does it take to remove tree roots from a sewer line?

acceptedAnswer.text: The time required to remove tree roots depends on the extent of the blockage and the method used. A straightforward hydro-jetting or snaking procedure might take 1 to 3 hours. If the sewer line is heavily damaged and requires excavation and repair, the process could take a full day or even several days. An inspection provides a more accurate timeline.
acceptedAnswer.description: Removal can take 1-3 hours for minor issues. If excavation and repair are needed, it could take a day or several days.
